name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,523

clue.text: Handle false bit of tooth chipped off at the back

indicators.note: something chipped off at the back has lost its tail, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: cod as an adjective means sham or mock, as in a cod accent
enamel is the hard outer layer of a tooth

explanation.surface: A broken false tooth with its back edge chipped away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a verb or a door fitting, but it is slang for a name; CODENAME is COD plus ENAMEL losing its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is informal slang for a name or alias, and a covert alias is exactly that.

clue.text: Poor creatures singer Charlotte found on highway outside of college

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two end letters, leaving the middle behind

blocks.note: Charlotte Church is a Welsh singer
the M1 motorway, written with I for 1
the first and last letters of college

explanation.surface: A singer spotted on the motorway outside a college.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway. 'Poor as a church mouse' is an old saying about extreme poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: Church mice are proverbially impoverished, from the saying that something is as poor as a church mouse.

clue.text: Exiles bound together climbing road going north

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading the word bound together upwards, from bottom to top
heading north in a down entry means the word for road is written bottom to top

blocks.note: tied with rope
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Prisoners chained together trudging north up a road into exile.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to deport them, so the verb in the third person matches.

clue.text: Loose morals in Spain become commonplace

indicators.note: loose suggests something no longer held in shape, so the letters are let free to rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Lax morality in Spain becoming routine.
explanation.definitionFit: To normalise is to make or become ordinary and usual, which is what commonplace means.

clue.text: Missing heads of senior military makes for nasty atmosphere

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: MIA stands for missing in action
first letters of senior and military

explanation.surface: Soldiers missing their senior officers creates a grim mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma, or miasm, is an unpleasant or unhealthy vapour or a heavy oppressive feeling in the air.

clue.text: Consort said to give encouragement

indicators.note: said tells us to listen to how the consort's name is spoken

blocks.note: Prince Philip was consort to Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A royal consort reported to boost morale.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or boost that perks someone up.

clue.text: 'elper with clues in Bury

indicators.note: the dropped aitch in this Cockney spelling signals that the opening H must be dropped too

blocks.note: someone who helps by giving clues gives hints

explanation.surface: A Cockney helper giving clues in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the town in Greater Manchester, but it is a verb. The apostrophe in 'elper shows a dropped aitch, which the answer drops too.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter is the formal word for placing a corpse in a grave or tomb, a synonym used at funerals.

clue.text: Sawn-off shooter fitted with silencer in case?

definitions.note: luggage is a collective noun covering cases

indicators.note: a sawn-off gun has had its end cut away, so the final letter goes
being fitted with something means taking it inside

blocks.note: a Luger is a German pistol
a gag silences someone

explanation.surface: A sawn-off gun with a silencer, ready just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooter' suggests any gun, but it is a particular German pistol. The question mark flags that a case is only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage is travellers' bags and suitcases taken together, of which a case is a typical item.

clue.text: Nuisance if clergyman loses grail regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of grail
the clergyman loses some letters, so they are taken out of him

blocks.note: a priest is a clergyman
second and fourth letters of grail

explanation.surface: A clergyman who mislays the Holy Grail would be an annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIEST with R and I removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is an irritating person or thing, the same as a nuisance.

clue.text: Limits to where bloggers insert endless pages online

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its boundaries, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Rules about where bloggers may put unlimited pages on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: A website is a collection of linked web documents published on the internet.

clue.text: Capital of Peru caps energy recycling

indicators.note: recycling reprocesses material into a new form, so these letters are remade

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Lima, Peru's capital, puts a cap on energy recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Peru' suggests Lima, but Capital is a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are also called upper-case letters, from the printer's upper type tray.

clue.text: Scapegoat beaten after removal of cloak and clothing

indicators.note: removal means taking the cloak's letters out of the word for scapegoat
something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
a cape is a cloak

explanation.surface: A scapegoat is beaten and stripped of cloak and clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The cloak sits as an unbroken run of letters inside the first word, which is why it can be lifted out cleanly.
explanation.definitionFit: Togas are the loose robes worn in ancient Rome, so they are garments.

clue.text: Witch cut and skinned cat roughly

indicators.note: a cut word has been docked, losing its last letter
a skinned word has lost its outer layer, leaving only its middle

blocks.note: Circe is the enchantress of Greek myth who turned Odysseus's men into pigs
the middle letter of cat

explanation.surface: A witch carving up and skinning a cat in rough fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa, from Latin, means approximately, used before dates and figures.

clue.text: Bad hearing with one standing in the wind

indicators.note: standing in a place means being inside it

blocks.note: the mistral is a strong cold wind of southern France
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone straining to hear out in the gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad hearing' suggests deafness, but a hearing here is a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistrial is a court trial rendered invalid by an error, so a legal hearing gone wrong.

clue.text: Person with remote control turned on old tripe

indicators.note: something turned has been twisted round, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone holding the TV remote switches on old rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripe also means nonsense, which fits the couch-potato picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone pilot flies an unmanned aircraft from a distance using a handheld controller.

clue.text: A language degree's the best

blocks.note: Master of Arts
taken as written
A1 means first-rate, written with I for 1

explanation.surface: A boast that a degree in languages is the finest qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Masai, also spelt Maa, is the tongue spoken by the Masai people of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Shot of rum gets attention of female astern

blocks.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
pronoun for a female
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A sailor with a tot of rum wins a woman's attention at the back of the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attention of female' gives HER EAR, so the female comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical term for behind the vessel, toward its back.

clue.text: Laundering machines relative put onto boats

blocks.note: a twin is a sibling
tub is slang for a slow, clumsy boat

explanation.surface: A relative is put on board some boats.
explanation.walkthrough: Tub is informal for a slow, tubby boat; in a down entry, put onto means the relative's letters come first.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-tub is an older type of washing machine with one drum to wash and a second to spin-dry.

clue.text: Unwelcome camera close, having zero range

blocks.note: a close is an end
O looks like zero
scope is extent or range

explanation.surface: A camera you don't want too close, with no range at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An endoscope is a medical instrument with a tiny camera, fed inside the body, which few patients enjoy.

clue.text: Slap delivered when lettuce quantities not right

indicators.note: not right means the letter standing for right is absent

blocks.note: cos is a variety of lettuce, known as romaine in the US
metrics are measures or quantities

explanation.surface: Someone slapped for getting the lettuce measurements wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slap' reads as a blow, but it is British slang for make-up. METRICS loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap is British informal for make-up, and cosmetics are face paint and powders.

clue.text: Monitor Five within secure centre of facility

indicators.note: within means placed inside the word for secure
the centre of a word is its middle letters

blocks.note: sure means safe or secure
Roman numeral five
the middle two letters of facility

explanation.surface: MI5 keeps watch on a secure facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monitor Five' suggests a screen, but Monitor is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To surveil is to keep watch on someone, especially covertly, which is to monitor them.

clue.text: See 23
One runs amongst the trees for protection

definitions.note: the definition is a mass noun; the answer is a plural of things giving it

indicators.note: amongst means placed among the letters of the trees

blocks.note: an, the indefinite article, means one
oaks are trees
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A jogger running among the trees for cover from the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoraks are hooded waterproof jackets worn to shield the wearer from wind and rain.

clue.text: Went on about naked hobo getting suspended sentence

indicators.note: about means going around the other piece
naked means stripped of its outer letters, keeping the middle

blocks.note: to prate is to talk on and on
the middle two letters of hobo

explanation.surface: Someone ranted about a naked tramp who got off with a suspended sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: Prate is an old word for chattering on foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being probated means being placed on probation, a court penalty served in the community instead of prison.

clue.text: Emigration supporter popular with Democrat has a downfall

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
in means fashionable or popular
D abbreviates Democrat
rain falls down

explanation.surface: A popular Democrat backer who suffers a fall from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a political backer, but it is a bra; 'downfall' suggests ruin, but it is rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain drain names the loss of skilled people when they move abroad for better jobs.

clue.text: I'm in the dark brown number

blocks.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown
NO is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Someone confused by a brown number in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunno is a casual contraction of don't know, an admission of not having a clue.

clue.text: Son Mark absorbed by recollection of belly dance

indicators.note: recollection is read as re-collection, gathering the word up again backwards
something absorbed is taken inside another thing

blocks.note: S abbreviates son
a pot, or pot belly, is a paunch
M abbreviates mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Mark's son is lost in memories of a belly dance.
explanation.walkthrough: POT reversed gives TOP, which takes in M.
explanation.definitionFit: The stomp is a lively jazz dance with heavy stamping steps.

clue.text: Police enclosures after duck stolen

indicators.note: something stolen has been taken away, so it vanishes from the word

blocks.note: coops are pens for poultry
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, written as O

explanation.surface: Officers investigate pens after a duck is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Cops is informal for police officers, and police can be plural.

clue.text: Conclusion of awesome gameplay

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, drawn from within the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: The finale of a brilliant video game.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet and so stands for the end of anything.

clue.text: Throw pig around entirely for two fat ladies here?

indicators.note: turning around means the word for pig faces the other way

blocks.note: to bin is to throw away
a hog is a pig
all means wholly

explanation.surface: Tossing a pig about wholesale, a scene for two hefty women.
explanation.walkthrough: Two fat ladies is the traditional bingo caller's phrase for number 88, from the shape of the digits.
explanation.definitionFit: A bingo hall is where bingo calls such as that rhyme for eighty-eight are heard.

clue.text: Farewell piece about heartless Lothario

indicators.note: about means going round the other piece
heartless means losing the middle, keeping only the outer letters

blocks.note: a song is a musical piece
first and last letters of Lothario

explanation.surface: A goodbye song about a heartless womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lothario is a seducer, named after a character in an 18th-century play.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is a casual way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Part of UK having considerable border finally arranged

indicators.note: finally means taking only the closing letter of border

blocks.note: some can mean considerable, as in some time
last letter of border
set means arranged

explanation.surface: A region of Britain with a large frontier being sorted out.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is a county in south-west England, and so a region within the United Kingdom.
